strengths: The panoramic interface is a coherent and useful contribution to 3D visual grounding: it combines scene-wide context with pretrained 2D VLMs while retaining a route to metric 3D localization. The camera placement, feature injection, and aggregation stages form a clearly motivated pipeline.

The strongest benchmark result is on Nr3D: single-dataset accuracy reaches 74.6%, compared with 69.9% for ViewSRD, with improvements across all reported subsets. ScanRefer also improves to 61.0% Acc@0.25, and the paper appropriately acknowledges that Sr3D performance is below the best competitor.

The generalization experiments provide meaningful evidence beyond standard benchmarks. With ground-truth instances supplied to all methods, the method achieves 53.5% on ARKitScenes and 43.8% on 3RScan. Its substantial gains on noun-free affordance queries and masked queries support improved robustness to implicit language.

The supplementary material adds useful camera-placement and test-time augmentation ablations, mesh-versus-3DGS comparisons, implementation details, and an explicit online runtime measurement. Separating single- and mixed-dataset training and identifying privileged semantic labels improve comparison transparency.
weaknesses: The central panorama-versus-pinhole comparison is insufficiently specified. Section 4.4 does not establish whether pinhole variants were separately fine-tuned on matching images with identical feature inputs, supervision, and aggregation. Without these controls, Table 4 cannot cleanly attribute the large advantage to panoramic context rather than adaptation or implementation differences.

Evidence for precise 3D localization is limited to ScanRefer Acc@0.25; Acc@0.5 is absent. Nr3D and the generalization experiments select among ground-truth instances, so their strong results do not validate the proposed box reconstruction stage. Stricter localization metrics and an aggregation ablation are particularly important for the claimed metric grounding capability.

The 'visibility-aware' aggregation in Section 3.4 filters points by whether they project inside the selected box, without specifying a depth-consistency or occlusion test. This can retain unrelated points along the same viewing rays. Denoising, panorama seam handling, and treatment of views where the target is absent are also insufficiently specified, making this stage difficult to reproduce and assess.

The EMD objective is numerically ordered at the digit level, but it does not preserve distance between complete coordinates across carry boundaries. For example, the deterministic weighted digit penalty between 199 and 200 is 199 despite a coordinate difference of one. The empirical gain is useful, but the interpretation as coordinate-distance-aware supervision needs qualification or comparison with a coordinate-level objective.

Some component claims exceed the evidence: geometric features reduce accuracy from 60.4% to 60.2% without geometric QA and add only 0.3 points with QA. No repeated-run variability is reported. Likewise, ordinary rephrasing performance remains below PQ3D, so the strongest language-robustness conclusion concerns removed class cues rather than uniformly superior paraphrase handling.

Generalization reproducibility needs exact evaluation subset sizes and selection rules, together with validation that generated query variants preserve the target and remain unambiguous. The reported 3.30-second runtime usefully covers online inference, but excludes scene preprocessing and lacks baseline cost comparisons, limiting the efficiency claim.

strengths: Assessed as Algorithms/General, the paper offers a useful representation-level contribution: panoramic images connect pretrained 2D grounding VLMs to 3D scenes while retaining broad relational context. The combination of camera placement, semantic feature fusion, and 3D lifting is coherent and relevant to computer vision.

The reported benchmark results support the approach. In Table 1, single-dataset Nr3D accuracy reaches 74.6 versus 69.9 for ViewSRD, with improvements across all reported Nr3D subsets. ScanRefer improves more modestly to 61.0 versus 60.0 for VGMamba. The paper appropriately acknowledges that it does not lead Sr3D.

Generalization experiments extend beyond standard benchmarks. With ground-truth instances supplied to all methods, Table 2 reports substantial ARKitScenes gains and useful improvements on 3RScan. Table 3 shows particularly strong performance when target names are removed: 51.7 versus PQ3D's 35.8 on affordance descriptions without object names.

The ablations provide meaningful evidence for several design choices. Panoramas outperform the tested non-oracle pinhole configurations; semantic features improve accuracy from 58.4 to 60.4; and structure-aware placement improves over random placement with the same average camera count, from 51.9 to 61.0. Supplementary experiments cover test-time rotations and mesh versus 3DGS representations.

The presentation is generally clear, with attribution of the pretrained models and borrowed components. The supplement supplies useful training, rendering, prompt, and runtime details. Overall, the empirical breadth and strong Nr3D results support a slight preference for acceptance.
weaknesses: The central panorama-versus-pinhole comparison is insufficiently specified. Section 4.4 does not clearly establish whether each pinhole configuration receives representation-matched fine-tuning, identical feature adapters and objectives, and comparable inference resources. This matters because four panoramic yaw rotations alone improve accuracy from 54.8 to 61.0. Table 4 supports the tested configurations, but does not fully isolate panoramic context as the cause of the gains.

Evidence for precise 3D localization is limited. ScanRefer reports only Acc@0.25, omitting the more demanding Acc@0.5. The cross-dataset experiments use ground-truth instances and the alternative selection-and-voting pipeline, so they do not validate generalization of the proposed free-form 3D box reconstruction. The visibility-aware aggregation itself lacks an ablation, despite being a core component.

The aggregation procedure leaves consequential implementation questions unresolved. Section 3.4 filters points by projection into the selected 2D box without specifying a depth-based visibility check, and leaves denoising unspecified. Treatment of panorama-seam crossings and predictions from views where the target is absent is also unclear; such absent-target examples are excluded during training. These details affect robustness and reproducibility.

Equation 3 is a valid per-digit Wasserstein loss against a point target, but the weighted sum is not a distance between complete numerical coordinates. Carry boundaries can make nearby coordinates receive large penalties: 499 versus 500 incurs a weighted digit distance of 199 despite a coordinate difference of one. The empirical 0.9-point gain is useful, but the numerical-distance interpretation needs qualification. Likewise, geometry adds only 0.3 points over semantic features plus geometric QA, without repeated-run uncertainty to establish that small gain.

The generalization claims need tighter scope and documentation. Exact evaluated scene/query counts and split definitions for the external datasets are not provided. Generated language variants have no reported human audit of referent preservation or ambiguity after noun removal. Moreover, PQ3D performs better on both original and rephrased queries, so the strongest language result concerns missing class cues rather than uniformly superior paraphrase robustness.

Practical efficiency is only partially characterized. The system uses a 17B backbone and averages 9.6 forward passes per query; the reported 3.30-second A100 runtime excludes camera selection, rendering, and semantic-field construction. These exclusions are disclosed, but preprocessing cost, memory requirements, and matched baseline runtimes are needed to substantiate broader efficiency claims.

strengths: The paper presents a coherent Algorithms/General contribution: panoramic renderings provide a useful interface between pretrained 2D VLMs and 3D grounding. Structure-aware camera placement, fused semantic features, and multi-view lifting form a well-motivated pipeline with potential relevance beyond grounding.

The Nr3D results are strong: single-dataset accuracy reaches 74.6%, compared with 69.9% for ViewSRD, and joint training improves this to 76.1%. The paper also reports competitive ScanRefer and Sr3D performance without requiring leadership on every benchmark.

The generalization experiments are valuable. With ground-truth instances supplied to all methods, the approach achieves 53.5% on ARKitScenes versus 36.1% for the strongest reported baseline. Gains over PQ3D on noun-free affordance queries (+15.9 points) and masked queries (+8.5 points) support improved handling of implicit language.

The experimental analysis extends beyond headline scores. Camera-placement ablations, panorama versus pinhole comparisons, modality ablations, rotation studies, and mesh/3DGS experiments provide useful evidence. The supplement also supplies training details, prompts, and online runtime.
weaknesses: The reported aggregate metrics need reconciliation. In Table 2, Overall should be a common weighted average of Unique and Multiple for a fixed evaluation set. ViL3DRel's 92.0/51.8/59.6 implies approximately 19.4% Unique queries, whereas BUTD-DETR's 92.5/52.6/58.5 implies 14.7% and MCLN's 93.4/54.9/60.6 implies 14.8%. These differences exceed rounding and are concerning because the table states that all baselines were rerun under a shared protocol. Evaluation counts, exclusions, and aggregation rules should be clarified before treating these comparisons as conclusive.

Evidence for precise, generalizable 3D box localization is incomplete. ScanRefer reports only Acc@0.25, omitting the stricter Acc@0.5 metric that would better test the lifting and fusion stage. Cross-dataset and language robustness experiments use ground-truth instances, establishing robustness of instance selection rather than end-to-end localization under distribution shift. The claims should distinguish these outcomes.

The central panorama comparison lacks sufficient protocol detail to isolate the representation's contribution. Section 4.4 does not clearly establish whether pinhole variants receive matched fine-tuning, feature adapters, training exposure, and inference budgets. This matters because four yaw augmentations alone raise panoramic accuracy from 54.8% to 61.0%. Moreover, the oracle target-centered view is not a strict upper bound for contextual pinhole grounding, since it can omit informative reference objects.

The EMD objective is valid as a digit-wise distance but does not faithfully represent coordinate distance across digit carries. For example, the weighted digit penalty between 199 and 200 is 199 despite a coordinate difference of one, whereas 199 versus 190 incurs only nine. This limits the numerical-distance interpretation, although the observed 0.9-point improvement remains useful empirical evidence. No repeated-run uncertainty is provided for this gain or the smaller geometric-feature improvements.

Several details affecting reproduction and practicality remain underspecified: panorama seam handling for boxes, point-cloud denoising, and depth-based occlusion handling during the stated visibility-aware fusion. The 3.30-second online runtime transparently excludes preprocessing, but reconstruction, feature extraction, camera selection, and storage costs are unreported. These dependencies qualify the efficiency and deployment claims.

strengths: Under Algorithms/General, the paper offers a useful and coherent contribution: panoramic renderings connect pretrained 2D VLMs to 3D grounding while retaining broad spatial context. Structure-aware viewpoint selection, feature adapters, and cross-view aggregation form a well-motivated pipeline.

The benchmark evidence supports acceptance. Single-dataset Nr3D accuracy reaches 74.6%, versus 69.9% for ViewSRD, with gains across all reported subsets. ScanRefer improves more modestly to 61.0% Acc@0.25 versus 60.0% for VGMamba. The paper appropriately separates single-dataset and mixed-dataset training.

The representation receives meaningful experimental support. Table 6 reports 61.0% for panoramas versus 51.0% for the strongest non-oracle pinhole configuration. Supplementary camera-placement ablations improve accuracy from 51.9% with random placement to 61.0% with the proposed strategy at the same average camera count.

Generalization experiments extend beyond standard benchmarks. With ground-truth instances supplied to all methods, ARKitScenes accuracy reaches 53.5%, substantially above the reported baselines. The noun-removal experiments also demonstrate useful robustness to descriptions that lack explicit class names.

The supplement provides substantial implementation details, backbone and runtime comparisons, reconstruction experiments, and informative failure analysis. Reporting reconstruction failures, preprocessing costs, and sensitivity to test-time rotations makes the practical limitations assessable.
weaknesses: The central panorama-versus-pinhole comparison needs clearer experimental controls. Table 6 does not explicitly establish whether pinhole models receive matched fine-tuning, feature adapters, geometric QA, image resolution, and aggregation. Test-time rotations alone raise panoramic accuracy from 54.8% to 61.0%, so matched training and inference budgets are important for attributing the gain specifically to panoramic context. Independently processing pinhole views also does not establish a fundamental limitation of approaches that jointly reason over multiple perspective images.

Evidence for accurate 3D box recovery is incomplete. ScanRefer reports only Acc@0.25, without the stricter Acc@0.5 metric, and the proposed visibility-aware aggregation lacks a direct ablation. Filtering points by membership in an anchor's projected bounding box does not itself enforce depth visibility, so unrelated geometry along the same rays can survive. These omissions matter for claims of precise metric localization.

The EMD objective is valid as a weighted sum of per-digit Wasserstein losses, but it does not preserve numerical proximity between complete coordinates across carry boundaries. For example, changing 499 to 500 incurs a weighted digit distance of 199 despite a coordinate displacement of one. The consistent 0.9-point improvement supports its empirical usefulness, but the distance-aware interpretation should be qualified or compared with a coordinate-level alternative. Smaller geometry-related gains also lack uncertainty estimates.

Generalization and deployment claims require narrower qualification. Cross-dataset evaluations use ground-truth instances and therefore establish transfer of object selection rather than the complete localization pipeline. The fully automatic reconstruction experiment retains only 92 of 141 validation scenes, and its comparison with the published LIFT-GS result uses different evaluation populations. The self-captured demonstration contains only two queries in one scene and requires substantial offline processing.

Several details remain unclear for reproduction and interpretation: treatment of targets crossing the panorama seam, exact visibility weights in ReferIt3D voting, and the configuration used for zero-shot evaluation. In particular, zero-initialized adapters contribute no semantic or geometric features without training, so Table 2 cannot straightforwardly substantiate the claimed benefit of the multi-modal representation unless a different initialization or feature-integration mechanism is specified.

strengths: The paper makes a useful Algorithms/General contribution: panoramic renderings provide a straightforward interface between pretrained 2D VLMs and 3D grounding, preserving broad scene context. Although many components are established, their integration is coherent and supported by experiments.

The strongest benchmark result is on Nr3D: single-dataset accuracy improves from ViewSRD’s 69.9% to 74.6%, with gains across all reported subsets (Table 1). ScanRefer improves more modestly, from 60.0% to 61.0% Acc@0.25. Separating single-dataset and mixed-dataset training improves comparison transparency.

The panorama hypothesis receives meaningful empirical support. Table 6 reports 61.0% accuracy versus 51.0% for the strongest non-oracle pinhole configuration, with larger advantages for descriptions mentioning more objects. Supplementary camera-placement experiments show 61.0% with approximately 2.4 selected cameras versus 51.9% with the same number of random cameras.

Generalization experiments extend beyond standard benchmark evaluation. With GT instances supplied to all methods, the approach achieves 53.5% on ARKitScenes and 43.8% on 3RScan, exceeding the reported baselines. Its advantages on noun-removed and noun-masked descriptions are also substantial, although ordinary paraphrasing does not outperform PQ3D.

The supplement substantially strengthens the submission through component ablations, smaller-backbone experiments, runtime and memory measurements, automated reconstruction experiments, and explicit failure cases. These support a weak acceptance despite the limitations below.
weaknesses: Evidence for precise free-form 3D localization is incomplete. ScanRefer reports only Acc@0.25, omitting the commonly reported Acc@0.5. Nr3D and the generalization experiments instead select among GT instances, bypassing the proposed free-form 3D aggregation. Stricter localization metrics and an ablation of anchor selection and fusion are needed to establish that this component reliably recovers object extent.

The panorama-versus-pinhole comparison leaves important controls unclear: whether pinhole variants are separately fine-tuned with equivalent supervision, how their auxiliary features are constructed, and whether total inference budgets are comparable. This matters because supplementary Fig. 8 shows that four yaw rotations raise panorama accuracy from 54.8% to 61.0%. The results support the complete pipeline more clearly than they isolate panoramic context as the sole cause.

Raw-RGB deployment claims require qualification. The automated reconstruction experiment retains only 92 of 141 validation scenes after registration failures, and its 55.1% accuracy is conditional on that selection. LIFT-GS’s cited 49.7% uses a different evaluation set, so that comparison does not establish superiority. The self-captured demonstration contains only two queries in one scene and requires approximately 154 minutes for reconstruction and semantic-feature lifting before subsequent processing.

The geometry and EMD contributions are less compelling than the main representation contribution. Geometry adds only 0.3 points when geometric QA is present and slightly hurts without it (Table 5); no repeated-run uncertainty is reported. Moreover, the weighted per-digit EMD is not a distance on complete coordinate values: a small coordinate change across a digit boundary can incur a large penalty. Its empirical benefit is useful, but the numerical-distance motivation should be stated more narrowly.

Some generalization and implementation details remain insufficiently specified. The cross-dataset evaluations lack exact evaluated scene/query counts and split descriptions; generated text variants lack a reported semantic-preservation audit. Panorama seam handling, segmentation configuration, and outlier-removal parameters are also unclear. These omissions affect reproducibility and interpretation, particularly because unseen targets are excluded during training and seam-crossing objects can produce unusually large 2D boxes.

strengths: As an Algorithms/General contribution, PanoGrounder offers a coherent and useful approach to transferring pretrained 2D VLMs to 3D grounding. The panoramic interface, structure-aware camera placement, and semantic feature fusion address concrete limitations of perspective-view pipelines.

The Nr3D results are compelling: single-dataset accuracy reaches 74.6%, compared with 69.9% for ViewSRD, and joint training increases it to 76.1%. The zero-shot result of 53.2% also supports the usefulness of the representation independently of task-specific fine-tuning.

The panorama comparison provides meaningful evidence for the central design choice: 61.0% versus 51.0% for 16 fixed pinhole views, with particularly strong results on descriptions mentioning several objects. Supplementary camera-placement ablations further show substantial improvements over random placement at comparable camera counts.

The generalization experiments extend beyond standard benchmarks. Gains on both Unique and Multiple subsets of ARKitScenes and 3RScan support transfer under ground-truth-instance evaluation. The strong performance when target nouns are removed is also valuable, although ordinary paraphrasing does not outperform PQ3D.

The supplement provides substantial implementation details, backbone scaling, test-time augmentation analysis, runtime measurements, and explicit failure cases. The automated reconstruction experiment and self-captured example strengthen the practical case, while the limitations discussion appropriately acknowledges reconstruction dependence and inference cost.
weaknesses: The reported ScanRefer aggregates raise a substantive comparability concern. In Table 1, Overall = p × Unique + (1−p) × Multiple implies a Unique fraction of approximately 19.7% for PanoGrounder but 14.0% for VGMamba. Table 3, despite stating that all baselines were rerun under the same setting, implies approximately 19.3% for PanoGrounder versus 14.8% for BUTD-DETR and MCLN. These differences exceed rounding error. Exact evaluated query sets, subset definitions, and aggregation rules are needed; the small ScanRefer state-of-the-art margin is not secure until this is resolved.

Localization quality is evaluated only at IoU 0.25 on ScanRefer. Acc@0.5 would be particularly informative because the method constructs boxes from segmented visible surfaces and acknowledges partial-object failures. There is also no direct ablation of the proposed visibility-aware aggregation against simpler fusion, while Nr3D and generalization experiments use a different instance-matching/voting procedure and therefore do not validate this component.

The panorama-versus-pinhole experiment does not clearly specify whether pinhole variants receive equivalent representation-specific fine-tuning, feature inputs, image resolution, and augmentation budgets. This matters because supplementary Fig. 8 shows that four yaw rotations alone raise accuracy from 54.8% to 61.0%. The comparison supports the complete pipeline more clearly than it isolates panoramic context.

Some methodological claims exceed the evidence. The digit-wise EMD is a valid ordinal loss per digit, but it is not a coordinate-level Wasserstein distance: numerical neighbors across carry boundaries, such as 199 and 200, incur large digit-wise penalties. Its empirical benefit is modest but consistent; the interpretation should be qualified. Likewise, geometric features provide only small gains, without repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

The strongest deployment and language-generalization claims require qualification. Automated reconstruction succeeds on only 92 of 141 validation scenes, and the cited LIFT-GS result uses a different evaluation population. Ground-truth instances simplify the cross-dataset setting, and no human audit establishes that generated language variants preserve the intended referent. These experiments remain useful, but do not establish unrestricted end-to-end generalization.
